question: Mile sur mera tumhara' become so popular as a National Integration Song that this line is inscribed on the Sawai Gandharva Memorial constructed by _________ in Pune.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhimsen Joshi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• ** Bhimsen Joshi**:

 
 
• **Pandit Bhimsen Gururaj Joshi **was one of the greatest **Indian vocalists from India **in the** Hindustani classical** tradition who constructed and inscribed the patriotic song "Mile Sur Mera Tumhara: on Sawai Gandharva Memorial in Pune.
 
• He is known for the **khayal** form of singing, as well as for his popular renditions of devotional music **(bhajans and abhangs)**.
 
• Joshi belongs to the** Kirana Gharana **tradition of Hindustani Classical Music.
 
• He was the** first musician** from India whose concerts were advertised through posters in** New York City**.
 
• Joshi was instrumental in organising the **Sawai Gandharva Music Festival** annually, as a homage to his** guru, Sawai Gandharva**.
 
• He received the** Bharat Ratna in 2009**.
 
 
 
• **Mile Sur Mera Tumhara Song**:
 
 
• The song "**Mile Sur Mera Tumhara" ** promotes **national integration and unity in diversity**.
 
• The concept for Mile Sur was developed in **1988** by** Lok Seva Sanchar Parishad **and promoted by** Doordarshan **(then India's sole TV broadcaster) and **India's Ministry of Information**.
 
• The song was composed by **Ashok Patki**.
 
• Mile Sur was telecast for the** first time **on **Independence Day, 1988**, after the telecast of the Prime Minister's speech from the **ramparts **of the **Red Fort**.​
